checks.label: Which physics the motion happens in

detail.medium_source: International Standard Atmosphere, sea level, 15 C, 101.325 kPa
detail.medium_caveat: Density falls with altitude. A flier at 3000 m has about 74 % of this density and a correspondingly higher minimum airspeed.
detail.boundaries: There is no sharp boundary. Re = 1 is the conventional marker for where viscous forces dominate inertial ones and Re ~ 1000 for where inertia dominates; between them both matter and neither limit applies. The scallop theorem is a statement about the STOKES limit (Re -> 0), and applying it at Re = 0.9 rather than Re = 0.001 is a judgement, so the check reports the number and says how far into the limit the design actually is.

checks.reading: Re runs from 0.856 to 3.424 across the stated ranges: creeping (viscous forces dominate) at one end, intermediate (neither limit applies) at the other.

checks.label: Purcell scallop theorem
checks.reading: the stroke is declared non-reciprocal (18 degrees of freedom), so the theorem does not forbid it at any Reynolds number.

checks.label: Stride or beat produces the stated speed

detail.cycle_hz_source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: step frequency asked of the design.
detail.distance_per_cycle_source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: net advance per tripod cycle.
detail.note: Distance per cycle is NET displacement per cycle, not the path length the appendage travels. A stroke that sweeps far and returns the body nowhere has a large path and a distance per cycle of zero -- which is the scallop theorem restated as arithmetic.

checks.label: Where this sits among legged animals

detail.formula: Fr = v^2 / (g L), with L the characteristic length the caller supplied
detail.source: Alexander RM, Jayes AS 1983, A dynamic similarity hypothesis for the gaits of quadrupedal mammals, J Zool (Lond) 201:135-152
detail.why_this_is_not_a_verdict: Equal Froude number is a NECESSARY condition for two animals to move in a dynamically similar way, and later work is explicit that it is not sufficient -- cursorial and non-cursorial mammals do not move similarly at equal Fr. The widely quoted walk-to-run transition at Fr = 0.5 is a human result. Turning any of that into a pass or a fail for an arbitrary clade would be borrowing a threshold across exactly the gap this repository keeps finding and removing, so this check reports the number and stops.

checks.reading: Fr = 1.02e-3 to 0.016. This places the design among legged animals of its size and says nothing about whether it can do it.

result.reading: nothing this layer can check contradicts the design. That is NOT a finding that it moves: there is no muscle here, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget, and 2 of the 4 checks are regime indicators that never fail anything.
what_this_layer_cannot_say: whether the organism can generate the forces its gait requires: there is no muscle model and no actuator model
whether it can pay for the motion: no metabolic rate, no cost of transport, no energy budget
whether it can control the motion or stay the right way up: no stability model
whether the gait is one a nervous system could produce or a developmental program could build

Purcell EM 1977, Life at low Reynolds number, Am J Phys 45(1):3-11, doi 10.1119/1.10903. A theorem about the Stokes limit, not a measurement of any organism.

result.scope: How a design moves, as distinct from what it is made of. One theorem (the scallop theorem, which can declare a design impossible), arithmetic over declared quantities, and empirical regime indicators that are reported and never fail anything. It models no muscle, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget: a design this layer does not contradict has not been shown to move, only shown not to be self-contradictory in the ways this layer can see.
